text: A remote backend fixes the no-shared-truth problem from Lesson 10, but it does nothing about timing on its own. Two engineers can both have that same backend configured correctly and both run terraform apply within the same thirty seconds against the same shared state — with no coordination between them, their writes can interleave and corrupt it, or one can simply overwrite the other's result an instant later.

State locking is the fix: before Terraform writes to state, it first acquires an exclusive lock, and anything else that needs to write has to wait until that lock is released. The azurerm backend locks automatically using Azure Blob Storage's native lease mechanism, with no extra config at all. The s3 backend has no equivalent built-in feature, so it relies on a separate DynamoDB table, added with one extra argument: dynamodb_table.

That DynamoDB table needs exactly one thing to work: a primary key named LockID, of type String. Terraform writes and deletes a row keyed on the state file's path to claim and release the lock. You can provision the table itself with a small bootstrap Terraform config that runs ahead of the main one, since the locking table obviously can't depend on the backend it exists to help lock.

Try to run apply while someone else's apply already holds the lock, and Terraform refuses outright rather than risk a collision, printing an error that names exactly who holds the lock, what operation they're running, and when they started it. That Who field is genuinely useful information — usually the right move on seeing it is simply to wait for their apply to finish, which releases the lock automatically.

Terraform does provide terraform force-unlock for the rare case a lock gets genuinely stuck, say after a crashed process that never released it cleanly, but running that command while an apply is still actually in progress is exactly the kind of state corruption this whole locking mechanism exists to prevent. Lesson 12 moves to a different state problem entirely: bringing infrastructure someone already created by hand under Terraform's management without recreating it.
